Kristian Edwards (born August 17, 1987) in Tampa, FL is an American public health scholar, entrepreneur, wellness advocate, and the founder of BLK + GRN, a marketplace featuring non-toxic, all-natural products created exclusively by Black women artisans. She is recognized for her work at the intersection of public health, conscious consumerism, and economic empowerment, and has been featured in major national media outlets including Forbes, Essence, Glamour, and Women’s Health.
Early life and education
Edwards was born in Tampa, Florida, to David and Nicole Henderson, and raised in Little Rock, Arkansas, where she attended Little Rock Central High School. She earned her bachelor’s degree from Yale University', majoring in the history of medicine and her Master of Health Policy and Administration. She later completed  and Doctor of Public Health (DrPH) in Health Management and Leadership at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.
Career
Academic and public health work
Edwards began her career in public health research and administration, focusing on health equity, environmental justice, and the social determinants of health. She later joined the faculty at George Washington University, where she taught courses in health policy, leadership, and adminstration.
BLK + GRN
In 2018, Edwards founded BLK + GRN, an e-commerce marketplace featuring non-toxic personal care and wellness products crafted by Black women artisans. The platform promotes conscious consumerism, sustainability, and economic empowerment. The BLK + GRN ecosystem is a thriving hub for non-toxic living, wellness education, and community empowerment driven by Black women artisans. It empowers conscious living through education, community, and commerce rooted in wellness and sustainability. Our platform supports economic growth within the Black community by promoting intentional, health-focused consumption and thoughts. When you buy Black and live green, you're investing in both personal and collective well-being.
BLK + GRN has been featured in major publications such as:
* Forbes, highlighting its mission and marketplace model
* Essence, for curation and wellness-centered home products
* Glamour, for advancing Black-owned wellness businesses
* Women’s Health, for her advocacy of clean beauty for Black women
* ABC News Live, highlighting Black-owned natural products
Her work has also been profiled in The Everygirl, CIO Today, Voyage Baltimore, The Grio, Blavity, HypeBae, Bustle, and Yellow Co.
Media contributions and thought leadership
Edwards has provided expert commentary on toxic-free living, sustainability, health equity, and conscious wellness. She has contributed to or been featured by:
* Redfin, discussing wellness-centered home environments
* Howard University News Service, in reporting on sustainability and the African diaspora
* Podcasts including Balanced Black Girl, Black Women Talk Work, The Jealous Vegan, and Alex Elle
She has written or contributed to wellness and lifestyle content in Radiant Health, In Her Shoes, Food Heaven Made Easy, and MILQ Magazine.
Personal health advocacy
Edwards is also a traumatic brain injury (TBI) survivor following a 2019 car accident and has used her platform to advocate for mental health, self-care, and workplace wellness.
Personal life
Edwards lives with her husband, Jason, and their two sons. Jason is a self-taught home chef who started taking cooking seriously when I realized that it was possible to eat restaurant-quality food in the comfort of my own home. She frequently speaks publicly about conscious parenting, intentional living, and generational wealth in Black families.
